title: Anticoagulation Risk Stratification for Spine Procedures
description: Guide for managing anticoagulant and antiplatelet therapy before interventional spine procedures, stratified by procedure risk tier.

procedure-risk.question: What is the bleeding risk tier of the planned procedure?
procedure-risk.body: Pain medicine societies stratify procedures into three risk tiers based on the potential consequences of bleeding.

options.label: Peripheral procedure (MBBs, peripheral joint injections, trigger points)
options.rationale: Low bleeding risk — bleeding can be identified and compressed

options.label: Intermediate procedure (TFESI, facet joint injections, SIJ injection)
options.rationale: Moderate risk — near neural structures but not neuraxial

options.label: Neuraxial procedure (interlaminar epidural, SCS lead placement)
options.rationale: High risk — epidural hematoma can cause permanent paralysis

procedure-risk.evidenceCitation: SIS/ASIPP risk stratification: Peripheral (low risk, compressible), Intermediate (near neural structures), Neuraxial (highest risk, epidural hematoma potential).

peripheral-approach.question: Peripheral Procedures — Generally Safe to Continue Anticoagulation
peripheral-approach.body: For peripheral procedures where bleeding can be visualized and compressed, evidence suggests that the thromboembolic risk of holding anticoagulation often exceeds the bleeding risk of continuing.

options.label: Patient on aspirin or NSAIDs
options.rationale: Continue — do not hold for peripheral procedures

options.label: Patient on warfarin or DOAC
options.rationale: Generally safe to continue — case-by-case assessment

options.label: Patient on dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT)
options.rationale: Increased bleeding risk but still manageable for peripheral procedures

peripheral-approach.evidenceCitation: IPSIS Task Force: Holding anticoagulation for peripheral procedures carries greater thromboembolic risk than the bleeding risk of continuing.

peripheral-continue.question: Continue Anticoagulation for Peripheral Procedures
peripheral-continue.outcome: Proceed with the peripheral procedure without holding anticoagulation. Use a 25-gauge needle to minimize bleeding. Monitor the injection site post-procedure. The risk of thromboembolic events from holding medication (stroke, PE, MI) exceeds the risk of a compressible bleed at the injection site.
peripheral-continue.evidenceCitation: Dr. O'Brien's practice: never holds anticoagulation for peripheral procedures. IPSIS supports this approach based on risk-benefit analysis.

peripheral-dapt.question: DAPT for Peripheral Procedures
peripheral-dapt.outcome: Dual antiplatelet therapy (aspirin + P2Y12 inhibitor) increases bleeding risk but peripheral procedures remain generally safe. Discuss with the prescribing cardiologist if concerned. Do NOT hold P2Y12 inhibitors without cardiology input, especially within 6 months of coronary stent placement.
peripheral-dapt.evidenceCitation: Holding P2Y12 inhibitors after recent coronary stent placement carries risk of stent thrombosis, which has ~40% mortality.

intermediate-approach.question: What anticoagulant/antiplatelet is the patient taking?
intermediate-approach.body: Intermediate-risk procedures require case-by-case assessment balancing bleeding risk against thromboembolic risk.

options.label: DOAC (apixaban, rivaroxaban, dabigatran, edoxaban)
options.rationale: May need to hold 1-2 days depending on renal function

options.label: P2Y12 inhibitor (clopidogrel, prasugrel, ticagrelor)
options.rationale: Coordinate with prescriber — hold time varies by agent

intermediate-aspirin.question: Aspirin for Intermediate Procedures
intermediate-aspirin.outcome: Continue aspirin monotherapy for intermediate-risk procedures. No evidence that holding aspirin reduces bleeding risk for these procedures, and stopping aspirin increases cardiovascular event risk.
intermediate-aspirin.evidenceCitation: Multiple guidelines support continuing aspirin for intermediate-risk spine procedures.

intermediate-warfarin.question: Warfarin for Intermediate Procedures
intermediate-warfarin.outcome: Check INR. If INR is within therapeutic range (typically <=3.0), many practitioners proceed with intermediate procedures. If INR is supratherapeutic, delay the procedure. The decision to hold warfarin requires individualized risk-benefit assessment considering the indication for anticoagulation (mechanical valve vs atrial fibrillation vs DVT prophylaxis). Coordinate with the prescribing physician.
intermediate-warfarin.evidenceCitation: UpToDate: Decisions regarding anticoagulant discontinuation should include a risk-benefit analysis considering why the patient is taking the anticoagulant.

intermediate-doac.question: DOAC for Intermediate Procedures
intermediate-doac.outcome: Consider holding for 1-2 half-lives (typically 24-48 hours for most DOACs). Adjust for renal function — dabigatran in particular requires longer hold times with CrCl <50. Resume 24 hours post-procedure if no complications. Bridging is NOT recommended for DOACs. Coordinate hold timing with the prescribing physician.
intermediate-doac.evidenceCitation: DOAC half-lives: apixaban ~12h, rivaroxaban ~5-9h, dabigatran ~12-17h (longer with renal impairment), edoxaban ~10-14h.

intermediate-p2y12.question: P2Y12 Inhibitor for Intermediate Procedures
intermediate-p2y12.outcome: Coordinate with the prescribing cardiologist. Typical hold times: clopidogrel 5-7 days, prasugrel 7-10 days, ticagrelor 5 days. CRITICAL: Do NOT hold within 6 months of bare metal stent or 12 months of drug-eluting stent placement without explicit cardiology approval — stent thrombosis risk is life-threatening.
intermediate-p2y12.evidenceCitation: Premature discontinuation of P2Y12 inhibitors after coronary stent placement is a major risk factor for stent thrombosis.

neuraxial-approach.question: What anticoagulant/antiplatelet is the patient taking?
neuraxial-approach.body: Neuraxial procedures carry the highest bleeding risk. Epidural hematoma, though rare, can cause permanent paralysis if not decompressed within 6-12 hours. Most guidelines recommend holding anticoagulation for neuraxial procedures.

options.label: Aspirin monotherapy
options.rationale: Most guidelines allow neuraxial procedures on aspirin

options.label: Warfarin
options.rationale: Must hold and verify normalized INR

options.label: Therapeutic heparin (IV or LMWH)
options.rationale: Must hold and verify normalized coagulation

neuraxial-approach.evidenceCitation: Epidural hematoma after neuraxial procedures manifests with progressive neurological deficit. Average time to full manifestation is ~3 hours. Decompression within 6-12 hours is critical for recovery.

neuraxial-aspirin.question: Aspirin for Neuraxial Procedures
neuraxial-aspirin.outcome: Most guidelines (ASRA, SIS) allow neuraxial procedures on aspirin monotherapy (81-325 mg). NSAIDs are also generally acceptable. However, aspirin combined with another anticoagulant requires holding the second agent per its specific guidelines.
neuraxial-aspirin.evidenceCitation: ASRA guidelines: aspirin monotherapy is not a contraindication to neuraxial procedures.

neuraxial-warfarin.question: Warfarin for Neuraxial Procedures — HOLD REQUIRED
neuraxial-warfarin.outcome: Hold warfarin for 5 days before the procedure. Verify INR is <=1.5 (some guidelines require <=1.2) on the day of the procedure. If the patient has a mechanical heart valve or high thromboembolic risk, coordinate bridging therapy with the prescribing physician. Resume warfarin the evening of the procedure if no complications.
neuraxial-warfarin.evidenceCitation: All major guidelines require holding warfarin and normalizing INR before neuraxial procedures.

neuraxial-doac.question: DOAC for Neuraxial Procedures — HOLD REQUIRED
neuraxial-doac.outcome: Hold for 3-5 half-lives before the procedure: apixaban hold 3 days, rivaroxaban hold 3 days, dabigatran hold 3-5 days (longer with renal impairment), edoxaban hold 3 days. No coagulation test reliably confirms DOAC clearance (anti-Xa levels may help for factor Xa inhibitors). Resume 24 hours post-procedure. Bridging is NOT recommended.
neuraxial-doac.evidenceCitation: ASRA guidelines: DOACs must be held for sufficient time to allow near-complete clearance before neuraxial procedures.

neuraxial-heparin.question: Heparin for Neuraxial Procedures — HOLD REQUIRED
neuraxial-heparin.outcome: IV heparin: hold 4-6 hours before, verify normalized aPTT. LMWH (therapeutic dose): hold 24 hours before. LMWH (prophylactic dose): hold 12 hours before. Resume heparin 1-2 hours post-procedure for IV, 24 hours for therapeutic LMWH. Monitor for signs of epidural hematoma for 24 hours post-procedure.
neuraxial-heparin.evidenceCitation: ASRA guidelines for heparin management around neuraxial procedures.
